title: The Bookkeeping Vault
pitch: Paperless-ngx turns a shoebox of scanned invoices and receipts into a searchable digital archive, but it doesn't know what any of those numbers mean or whether they add up. Anthropics' financial-services agents, particularly the GL Reconciler and Month-End Closer, know exactly how to find breaks, trace root causes, and draft accruals and commentary, but they need clean, structured documents to work from. Wire the two together: every scanned receipt and invoice lands in Paperless-ngx, gets tagged and OCR'd, and then an AI reconciliation agent reads the archive each month to flag mismatches and draft the close before a human bookkeeper signs off. The buyer is a small accounting practice or a solo bookkeeper serving several small-business clients, who can now offer 'AI-reviewed monthly books' as a premium tier without hiring another staff accountant.
why_now: Both trended today from opposite ends of the same back-office problem: one captures and archives the paperwork, the other reasons about the numbers inside it. Neither is a finished bookkeeping product alone, but together they cover the whole pipeline from paper to reconciled books.
